column7: Reads an untrusted peer's SSE stream up to its endpoint event and refuses past a 64 KiB handshake cap; the endpoint is resolved through the same-origin check (resolve_message_url), so no POST goes to another origin; later frames are bounded by MAX_PENDING_SSE_BYTES.
Refuses a request when the channel has ended or TAP_CAPACITY requests already wait: a capacity cap that decides allow or deny (the stricter tier applies).
Hands each response frame from the peer only to the waiting request with its id. The calls stream is shared by every caller of the backend, so a misroute would deliver one caller's answer to another.
The pairing key route and register decide on (the id's JSON text, so 1 and "1" differ); a private helper that makes route's decision.
Gates every SSE-mode call: a dead stream is replaced first, and a failed replacement refuses the call before its POST; nothing is resent.
The body of live_sse_channel: makes its replace-or-refuse decision.
Sends a listener request only with the credential its CredentialSource lends; a source that refuses means nothing is sent, never a send without the credential (MIK-8833's seam).
Registers each listener request on this session's own stream and POSTs it to that stream's endpoint only, so an answer or a request never crosses sessions.
Builds a listener request's headers and removes the calls' MCP-Session-Id, so the listener never speaks in the calls' session; a mistake would let it.
Builds the listener session (GET, endpoint, initialize, initialized) through send and SseChannel::open, which enforce; refuses a second open.
Builds the listener's own session with its credential once the SSE handshake is detected; the fail-closed rule for an identity credential is pick_session's (src/events).
